from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            'Meet our drone. It moves along two specific vectors.', 
            'We can scale these vectors by any amount.', 
            'Adding these scaled vectors creates a "linear combination."', 
            'By stretching and tip-to-tail placement, we reach targets.', 
            'This "recipe" defines every position the drone can hit.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & Linear Combinations", lecture_lines)

        # Coordinate System Setup
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_width": 2}
        )
        # Position plane in the 6x6 grid area
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        origin = plane.c2p(0, 0, 0)

        # Vector Definitions
        vec_a_color = "#FFD700" # Gold
        vec_b_color = "#87CEEB" # Sky Blue
        scaled_a_color = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        scaled_b_color = "#FF4500" # Orange-Red
        resultant_color = "#FFFFFF" # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(vec_a_color)
        
        vec_a = Arrow(start=origin, end=plane.c2p(1, 1, 0), buff=0, color=vec_a_color)
        vec_b = Arrow(start=origin, end=plane.c2p(1, 0, 0), buff=0, color=vec_b_color)
        
        label_a = Text("A", color=vec_a_color, font_size=24)
        label_b = Text("B", color=vec_b_color, font_size=24)
        
        # Position labels using grid
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(vec_a), 
            GrowArrow(vec_b), 
            Write(label_a), 
            Write(label_b), 
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(scaled_a_color)
        
        # Scale A to 2A
        vec_a_target = Arrow(start=origin, end=plane.c2p(2, 2, 0), buff=0, color=scaled_a_color)
        label_2a = Text("2A", color=scaled_a_color, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_2a, 'B6', scale_factor=0.7) # Fixed Issue 30

        self.play(
            Transform(vec_a, vec_a_target),
            Transform(label_a, label_2a),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(scaled_b_color)
        
        # Scale B to -1B
        vec_b_target = Arrow(start=origin, end=plane.c2p(-1, 0, 0), buff=0, color=scaled_b_color)
        label_nb = Text("-1B", color=scaled_b_color, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_nb, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8) # Fixed Issue 28

        self.play(
            Transform(vec_b, vec_b_target),
            Transform(label_b, label_nb),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(scaled_b_color)
        
        # Shift B tip-to-tail
        target_pos = vec_a.get_end()
        shift_vector = target_pos - vec_b.get_start()
        
        # Prepare moved label for B3
        label_nb_moved = Text("-1B", color=scaled_b_color, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_nb_moved, 'B3', scale_factor=0.7) # Fixed Issue 29
        
        self.play(
            vec_b.animate.shift(shift_vector),
            Transform(label_b, label_nb_moved),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(resultant_color)
        
        # Final resultant vector
        vec_c = Arrow(start=origin, end=vec_b.get_end(), buff=0, color=resultant_color)
        label_c = Text("2A - B", color=resultant_color, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8) # Fixed Issue 29 (part 2)

        self.play(
            Create(vec_c),
            Write(label_c),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'The "Span" is the set of all reachable points.',
            'Scale vectors infinitely to paint the entire territory.',
            'Two non-parallel vectors span an entire 2D plane.',
            "If vectors point the same way, we're stuck.",
            'They only span a single line in that case.'
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("The Span: The Reachable Territory", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        u_color = "#98FB98"  # Pale Green
        v_color = "#FF6347"  # Tomato
        grid_color = "#A9A9A9"  # Grey
        flash_color = "#FFFFFF"

        # Coordinate system setup for right-side visual area (A1-F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"stroke_width": 1, "include_tip": False, "color": GREY_E}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Vectors
        u_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1, 0.5), buff=0, color=u_color)
        v_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0.5, 1.5), buff=0, color=v_color)
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' executable dependency
        u_label = Text("u", color=u_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        v_label = Text("v", color=v_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        
        # Grid setup
        span_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": grid_color,
                "stroke_width": 1,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.4
            }
        )
        self.place_in_area(span_grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        u_label.next_to(u_vec.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v_label.next_to(v_vec.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(u_vec), Write(u_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Lines extending vectors
        u_line = Line(axes.c2p(-3, -1.5), axes.c2p(3, 1.5), color=u_color, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.6)
        v_line = Line(axes.c2p(-1, -3), axes.c2p(1, 3), color=v_color, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.6)

        self.play(Create(u_line), Create(v_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Flash effect
        flash_rect = Rectangle(
            width=5, height=5, 
            fill_color=flash_color, fill_opacity=0.4, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        self.place_in_area(flash_rect, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(span_grid))
        self.play(FadeIn(flash_rect), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(FadeOut(flash_rect), run_time=0.6)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # New target for v to make it collinear with u
        new_v_end = axes.c2p(2, 1)
        new_v_line = Line(axes.c2p(-3, -1.5), axes.c2p(3, 1.5), color=v_color, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.6)
        
        self.play(
            v_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(axes.c2p(0, 0), new_v_end),
            v_label.animate.next_to(new_v_end, UR, buff=0.1),
            FadeOut(span_grid),
            FadeOut(v_line),
            ReplacementTransform(v_line.copy(), new_v_line),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Emphasize the single line
        span_path = Line(axes.c2p(-3, -1.5), axes.c2p(3, 1.5), color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(Create(span_path))
        self.play(Indicate(span_path, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        lecture_lines = [
            'A set is dependent if a vector is redundant.',
            'One vector can be built from the others.',
            'This helper adds no new territory to our span.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper", lecture_lines)

        # Shared assets for vector positions
        # Origin at D2
        origin = self.grid['D2']
        x_target = self.grid['B3']
        y_target = self.grid['D4']
        
        vec_x_dir = x_target - origin
        vec_y_dir = y_target - origin
        
        # Define plane (parallelogram) corner
        plane_corner = origin + vec_x_dir + vec_y_dir
        
        # Load helper asset
        helper_icon = SVGMobject("/mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/helper.svg", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(helper_icon, 'A5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#DA70D6"))
        
        # Vectors x and y creating a plane
        vec_x = Arrow(origin, x_target, color="#DA70D6", buff=0)
        vec_y = Arrow(origin, y_target, color="#20B2AA", buff=0)
        
        label_x = Text("x", color="#DA70D6", slant=ITALIC)
        # Fix Issue 36: label_x at A2 to avoid overlap with arrowhead
        self.place_at_grid(label_x, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        label_y = Text("y", color="#20B2AA", slant=ITALIC)
        # Fix Issue 35: label_y at D6 for better proximity
        self.place_at_grid(label_y, 'D6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Creating a plane represented by a parallelogram
        plane = Polygon(origin, x_target, plane_corner, y_target, 
                       fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1, color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_x), Write(label_x))
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_y), Write(label_y))
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#20B2AA"))
        
        # Vector z resting exactly on that plane (z = 0.6x + 0.4y)
        z_target = origin + 0.6 * vec_x_dir + 0.4 * vec_y_dir
        vec_z = Arrow(origin, z_target, color="#FF0000", buff=0)
        
        label_z = Text("z", color="#FF0000", slant=ITALIC)
        # Fix Issue 34: label_z at C4 to avoid body overlap
        self.place_at_grid(label_z, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_z), Write(label_z))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Flash z and show it is a sum of scaled x and y
        # [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/helper.svg] integration
        self.play(Indicate(vec_z, color="#FF0000"), FadeIn(helper_icon))
        
        # Show components
        scaled_x_pt = origin + 0.6 * vec_x_dir
        vec_x_comp = Arrow(origin, scaled_x_pt, color="#DA70D6", stroke_width=3, buff=0)
        vec_y_comp = Arrow(scaled_x_pt, z_target, color="#20B2AA", stroke_width=3, buff=0)
        
        self.play(Create(vec_x_comp))
        self.play(Create(vec_y_comp))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Linear Independence: The Essential Team"
        lines = [
            'Vector P starts our journey by spanning a line.',
            'Adding vector Q expands our span into a plane.',
            'Vector R jumps our reach into 3D space.',
            'These independent vectors never overlap or repeat directions.',
            'No vector here is a combination of the others.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Vector Definitions
        p_color = "#7B68EE"
        q_color = "#FFDAB9"
        r_color = "#ADFF2F"
        span_2d_color = "#A9A9A9"
        
        origin_pt = ORIGIN
        p_vec = np.array([1.5, 0.2, 0])
        q_vec = np.array([0.5, 1.5, 0])
        r_vec = np.array([-1.2, 0.8, 0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Vector P starts our journey by spanning a line.
        
        vec_p = Arrow(origin_pt, p_vec, color=p_color, buff=0)
        label_p = Text("p", color=p_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(vec_p.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # 1D Span: A line through origin
        span_1d = Line(p_vec * -2, p_vec * 2, color=p_color, stroke_opacity=0.3)
        
        group_1d = VGroup(span_1d, vec_p, label_p)
        self.place_in_area(group_1d, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8) # Issue 38 Fix

        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(p_color),
            FadeIn(span_1d),
            GrowArrow(vec_p),
            Write(label_p),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Adding vector Q expands our span into a plane.
        
        vec_q = Arrow(origin_pt, q_vec, color=q_color, buff=0)
        label_q = Text("q", color=q_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(vec_q.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # 2D Span: A parallelogram (plane)
        span_2d = Polygon(
            (p_vec + q_vec) * -1.5,
            (p_vec - q_vec) * 1.5,
            (p_vec + q_vec) * 1.5,
            (q_vec - p_vec) * 1.5,
            fill_color=span_2d_color,
            fill_opacity=0.2,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        
        vis_group = VGroup(span_1d, span_2d, vec_p, vec_q, label_p, label_q)
        self.place_in_area(vis_group, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8) # Issue 38 Fix

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(q_color),
            FadeIn(span_2d),
            GrowArrow(vec_q),
            Write(label_q),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Vector R jumps our reach into 3D space.
        
        vec_r = Arrow(origin_pt, r_vec, color=r_color, buff=0)
        label_r = Text("r", color=r_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(vec_r.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        final_vis_group = VGroup(span_1d, span_2d, vec_p, vec_q, vec_r, label_p, label_q, label_r)
        self.place_in_area(final_vis_group, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8) # Issue 37 Fix

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(r_color),
            GrowArrow(vec_r),
            Write(label_r),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # These independent vectors never overlap or repeat directions.
        
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        # Pulse p, q, and r sequentially in white (#FFFFFF)
        for v in [vec_p, vec_q, vec_r]:
            self.play(Indicate(v, color=WHITE, scale_factor=1.2), run_time=0.8)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # No vector here is a combination of the others.
        
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        combo_p = vec_p.copy().set_color(WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        combo_q = vec_q.copy().set_color(WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.5).shift(p_vec)

        self.play(

        self.play(

            FadeOut(combo_p),

            FadeOut(sum_vec),
            FadeOut(not_equal),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration

        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They are linearly independent, meaning no redundant directions.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Pulse i and j in white
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            vec_j.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.set_color(COLOR_I),
            vec_j.animate.set_color(COLOR_J)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Together, they span and define the entire coordinate space.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_BASIS))

        # Target point and scaling logic
        target_coords = (2, 1)
        target_point_abs = plane.coords_to_point(*target_coords)
        target_dot = Dot(target_point_abs, color=WHITE)
        
        # Visualizing the span to reach target point
        vec_i_scaled = Arrow(
            plane.coords_to_point(0,0), plane.coords_to_point(2,0),
            buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4, stroke_opacity=0.6
        )
        vec_j_scaled = Arrow(
            plane.coords_to_point(2,0), plane.coords_to_point(2,1),
            buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4, stroke_opacity=0.6
        )

        # Labels anchored to grid
        formula_label = Text("2v1 + 1v2", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_label, 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        span_label = Text("Span{v1, v2}", font_size=24, color=COLOR_GRID)
        self.place_at_grid(span_label, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Show scaling and coverage
        self.play(
            Create(vec_i_scaled),
            Create(vec_j_scaled),
            FadeIn(target_dot),
            Write(formula_label),
            Write(span_label)
        )
        
        # Basis Toolkit integration
        toolkit = SVGMobject(TOOLKIT_PATH)
        self.place_at_grid(toolkit, 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        basis_tag = Text("Basis", font_size=32, color=COLOR_BASIS)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_tag, 'D6', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(toolkit),
            Write(basis_tag),
            Flash(basis_tag, color=COLOR_BASIS)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The DNA of Space: Understanding Span, Independence, and Bases
outline.target_audience: University undergraduates or advanced STEM high school students

sections.title: Prerequisites & Linear Combinations
sections.content: Introduce the basic building blocks: vector scaling and addition. Define a 'Linear Combination' as the result of scaling two or more vectors and adding them together. Visually, this is shown as stretching vectors and placing them tip-to-tail.
sections.example: Imagine a drone that can only move in two directions: Vector A (diagonal up-right) and Vector B (horizontal right). By scaling A and B (e.g., 2A + (-1)B), the drone can reach a specific landing pad. This 'recipe' is a linear combination.

sections.title: The Span: The Reachable Territory
sections.content: Define 'Span' as the set of all possible points reachable through linear combinations of a given set of vectors. Use animation to show vectors scaling infinitely to 'paint' a line or a plane.
sections.example: If our drone has two vectors that aren't on the same line, the 'Span' is the entire 2D floor. If the two vectors point in the same direction, the 'Span' is just a single line, and the drone is stuck in a 1D world.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
sections.content: Introduce the concept of redundancy. If one vector in a set can be created by a combination of the others, it adds no 'new' territory to the span. This set is 'Linearly Dependent.' Graphics should show a 3rd vector lying perfectly on the plane created by two others.
sections.example: Think of a search party of three robots. Robot C is 'dependent' if its search path can already be covered by combinations of Robot A and Robot B's paths. Robot C is redundant for exploring new dimensions.

sections.title: Linear Independence: The Essential Team
sections.content: Define 'Linear Independence' as a set where no vector can be built from the others. Each vector provides a unique direction that expands the span's dimensionality. Visually, adding an independent vector jumps from a 1D line to a 2D plane, or a 2D plane to 3D space.
sections.example: In a 3D video game, you need three independent movements: Forward/Back, Left/Right, and Up/Down. If 'Up' was just a mix of 'Forward' and 'Left', you could never actually jump—you'd be trapped on the ground.

sections.title: The Basis: The Efficient Blueprint
sections.content: Combine the previous concepts to define a 'Basis.' A basis is a set of vectors that are both Linearly Independent (no waste) and Span the entire space (complete coverage). It is the 'minimalist toolkit' for a vector space.
sections.example: Consider a LEGO set. A 'Basis' is the minimum number of unique brick types needed to build every possible model in the instruction manual. In the Cartesian plane, the unit vectors i (1,0) and j (0,1) are the most famous basis—simple, efficient, and they cover everything.

improvements.problem: The label '-1B' at 00:07 overlaps with the horizontal grid axis, making the text difficult to distinguish from the grid lines.
In the final sequence (00:12), the moved label '-1B' and the formula '2A - B' both occupy position A4, causing a significant overlap.
The label '2A' at 00:05 is positioned at A5, which is at the extreme upper edge of the grid, creating poor top-margin spacing.
The coordinate axes are at default scale in the A1-F6 area, causing the horizontal axis to crowd the left-side lecture notes and the top of the grid to press against the title.

The span grid at default scale fills the entire right quadrant, which makes the coordinate lines too dominant and causes the spanning line in the final scene to extend to the very edges of the screen.
The flash rectangle lacks a buffer margin, making the highlighting effect for the 'territory' feel unrefined and potentially overlapping with the title boundary.
The label 'label_z' at C3 overlaps the body of the red vector, obscuring the visual representation of the vector.
The label 'label_y' at E4 is positioned too far below the teal vector, losing visual proximity to the vector's tip.
The label 'label_x' at B2 directly overlaps the arrowhead of the purple vector.
The 3D visualization group ('final_vis_group') obstructs the lecture notes on the left side, specifically where vector 'r' and its label overlap the text.
Consistency issue: The initial and intermediate visual groups ('group_1d', 'vis_group') are positioned too close to the center, leading to the eventual obstruction.
improvements.solution: Line 78: self.place_in_area(group_1d, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8); Line 109: self.place_in_area(vis_group, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)

improvements.problem: The formula 'not_equal' at F4 is crowded by the animation area, creating visual clutter at the bottom of the display.
The main coordinate grid and vector display lack explicit anchoring, which can lead to misalignment with the left-side lecture notes.
The 'Span[v1, v2]' descriptive label is positioned at the bottom of the animation area without grid constraints, risking it being cut off.
The linear combination formula '2v1 + 1v2' is a long label that currently floats unanchored, which may lead to overlapping with grid lines.
